analyses.failure: test_chk_028_reset_during_traffic [slv_slow.s1] — AssertionError 'CHK-031: transfer 1 has no completion edge C' raised by score(e, partial=True) at test_async_apb_bridge.py:960 -> :553, right after a reset was asserted mid-traffic. It fails only in slv_slow.s1. The same test passes in the other 13 runs (results.json:396-425), and every SVA (CHK-001..CHK-017) shows fails=0 in slv_slow.s1 (sim_runs/slv_slow.s1.log:525-542).
analyses.spec_says: The spec only requires a transfer to be lost if it is still in flight when the reset is asserted. REQ-RESET-002 (spec/AsyncAPBBridge_Design_Specification.md:149; rules.json:1425 AB2-3-39): "The two resets shall be asserted together ... A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost." OP-008 (spec:428; rules.json:4776): "Asynchronous clear of the state of the domain ... transfer in flight lost". CHK-028 expected (contract.json:864): "The interrupted transfer never produces o_apb_pready. Each repeated transfer and all later traffic pass the CHK-029 scoreboard." CHK-031 (contract.json:947-948) defines C as "the i_clk_slv edge where o_apb_psel=1, o_apb_penable=1 and i_apb_pready=1 are sampled" and requires o_apb_pready to "become 1 at the j-th rising edge of i_clk_mst after C, with j in [N+1, N+3]". So with a fast mst clock and a slow slv clock, the requester legally gets PREADY well within one slv period after C. Nothing in the spec says a transfer that already returned PREADY is lost if a reset comes later.
analyses.rtl_does: Two-phase completion in RTL. At slv edge C, w_done = (state==ACCESS) & i_apb_pready (rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:139). This toggles reg_ack (slv.sv:176-179, 197-204) and loads reg_resp_hold (slv.sv:224-229). The ack crosses through u_sync_ack (rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst.sv:268-277). In WAIT, w_ack_event = (w_ack_s == reg_req) (mst.sv:137) drives w_load_resp (mst.sv:184-186), so reg_pready is 1 for exactly one mst cycle (mst.sv:215, 242). PREADY therefore arrives N+1..N+3 mst edges after C, plus the +APBCDC_MSYNC_EN model's extra stages (slv_slow.s1.log:481-483). With N=2 and T_mst=10 ns, that is about 30-50 ns after C. RTL acks only on a real completer handshake: reg_ack changes only on w_done, which needs ACCESS and i_apb_pready=1 at a slv rising edge. Reset asserts asynchronously and clears both FSMs, reg_ack/reg_req and the payload registers (slv.sv:186-229, mst.sv:199-238). The RTL behaviour seen is consistent with the spec. In slv_slow.s1, CHK-003/004/005/006 (PREADY in Access, one-cycle pulse, at most one PREADY per Setup) and CHK-013/014/015 all show 0 fails (slv_slow.s1.log:528-540). That argues against a spurious PREADY.
analyses.test_does:
Stimulus: 30 iterations, each with 12 random items (test:947-949). mid_time() polls at the fast clock's falling edge (mst here) until e.ndone()>=base and e.match(ph) (test:950-951). Phase 'pready' matches as soon as the requester has seen PREADY (test:171, req.state set to 'pready' at test:272). assert_resets() then drives both resets low (test:510-519), and score(e, partial=True) runs at once (test:960).

score(partial=True) keeps only requests that have tP, i.e. the requester saw PREADY (test:539, tP set at test:269). For each one it requires cpls[n] to contain both 'resp' and 'tC' (test:553). The expected value comes from the TB completer, not from the DUT.

How the completer model records completion:
- 'resp' is set at the falling slv edge before C, when it drives i_apb_pready=1 (test:389-392).
- 'tC' is set only at the next falling slv edge, after C has occurred (test:364-370: `if pps == 1 and ppe == 1 and self.drv_rdy and self.cur is not None: c['tC'] = t`).
- But at test:333-336 every falling edge that sees i_rst_n_slv=0 or i_rst_n_mst=0 calls reset_state() and `continue`s before line 364. So if the reset lands between C and the next falling slv edge, 'tC' is never written.

Why this only bites with a slow slv clock: the falling edge after C is C + T_slv/2. The slv start delay of 89.97 ns (slv_slow.s1.log:423) points to T_slv of roughly 90 ns, but the exact period is not in the files. With T_slv around 90 ns, C + T_slv/2 is about 45 ns, while the requester samples PREADY at about C + j*T_mst + T_mst/2, i.e. 35-55 ns. So the requester can record tP and the 'pready' phase can fire the reset before the completer has recorded tC. With the default 23.7 ns or a fast slv clock, T_slv/2 is under N+1 mst cycles, so tC is always recorded first. That fits the failure appearing only in slv_slow.s1.

candidates.evidence_for:
1) The completion edge C is a rising slv edge, but the TB records tC half a slv period later (test:364-366). The reset branch at test:333-336 runs before that and drops the record (reset_state() + continue), so a transfer that really completed loses its tC.
2) The reset trigger in phase 'pready' (test:171, 950-952) fires right after the requester sees PREADY. With a slow slv clock that is legally (CHK-031 j window, contract.json:948) before the completer's next falling edge.
3) Fails only in slv_slow.s1; passes in apb4.s1-s3, slv_fast.s1, sync3/4, 4ph etc. (results.json:396-425). That is the clock-ratio pattern a TB sampling race would produce.
4) The requester did get PREADY (tP present, filter at test:539). In RTL, PREADY needs reg_ack to toggle (mst.sv:137, 184-186, 215), which needs w_done = ACCESS & i_apb_pready (slv.sv:139, 178-179). In ACCESS the TB only drives i_apb_pready=1 at test:389-392, where 'resp' is also set. So the slv-side completion did happen; only the TB bookkeeping is missing.
5) No SVA failed in slv_slow.s1 (slv_slow.s1.log:525-542), including CHK-006 (at most one PREADY per Setup) and CHK-015 (transfer ends at the PREADY edge).
candidates.evidence_against:
1) The message checks 'resp' and 'tC' together (test:553), so the log does not prove which key was missing. Reasoning from the RTL and TB says it is 'tC', but no waveform or trace is available.
2) The exact slv_slow clock periods are not in the provided files. The timing argument rests on the slv start delay (89.97 ns) and on the CHK-031 window.
3) The failing iteration and phase cannot be identified from the log.

candidates.evidence_for: If the bridge gave the requester a PREADY without the completer finishing a transfer (a spurious ack toggle, e.g. a reg_req/reg_ack reset mismatch after a staggered release in an earlier iteration), cpls[1] would exist with no 'resp'/'tC' and the same message would appear. CHK-028 also stresses the reset/handshake state that such a bug would affect.
candidates.evidence_against:
1) reg_ack changes only on w_done (slv.sv:176-182), and w_done needs state==ACCESS and i_apb_pready=1 (slv.sv:139). Both reg_req and reg_ack reset to 0 together (mst.sv:208-209, slv.sv:198-199), so after release with no Setup there is no ack event.
2) The TB's per-cycle checks raised nothing before score() (otherwise a different message would appear): CHK-006 count at test:441, the quiet check at test:415 and 330, and the PREADY-while-pending checks at test:265-266.
3) All SVA in slv_slow.s1 report fails=0, including CHK-003/004/005/006 for the requester side and CHK-012..017 for the completer side (slv_slow.s1.log:525-542).
4) The same RTL passes the same test in 13 other runs and passes CHK-029 at 10:90 and 90:10 ratios.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says only 'a transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost' (spec:149, 292, 428). It does not say whether a transfer is still 'in flight' once the requester has sampled PREADY but the reset arrives before the slv-side cycle after C. The contract also does not say at which instant C must be recorded relative to an asynchronous reset.
candidates.evidence_against: CHK-031 defines C as a rising i_clk_slv edge sampled with resets high (contract.json:947). After PREADY the transfer is complete on both sides, so it is not 'in flight', and the scoreboard is right to expect it scored. The real question is when the TB samples C, not a spec ambiguity.

analyses.options:
1) Fix the test (recommended). Record the completion edge at the rising slv edge where it happens, not half a period later. Either option below keeps the check at full strength.
   a) Add a monitor on RisingEdge(i_clk_slv), with a ReadOnly/sample step, that sets cur['tC'] = now() when i_rst_n_slv=1, i_rst_n_mst=1, o_apb_psel=1, o_apb_penable=1 and i_apb_pready=1.
   b) In Completer.run, before the reset early-exit at test:333-336, finalize a pending completion. If pps==1, ppe==1, drv_rdy==1 and cur is not None, and both resets were still high at the rising edge e.es[-1] (record the reset level at each rising edge in _rec, or keep the reset-assert time from assert_resets and require it to be after e.es[-1]), then set cur['tC']=e.es[-1] and ackx, and only then call reset_state().
   Score() and the 'pready' reset phase stay unchanged. Re-run slv_slow.s1 with seed 1 to confirm.
2) Fix the RTL: no change is indicated. If the designer wants to rule out a spurious ack, dump a waveform of slv_slow.s1 around 2312.6-2342.0 us (slv_slow.s1.log:421-424) and check that the last o_apb_pready before the reset follows a slv edge with u_vlsit_apbcdc_slv in ACCESS and i_apb_pready=1.
3) Clarify the spec (optional). Add a sentence to REQ-RESET-002/ERR-003 saying that a transfer whose requester PREADY has already been sampled is complete and not 'lost', even if the reset comes before the next completer-side cycle. Also make clear that C is the rising i_clk_slv edge with both resets high. This makes the TB fix in option 1 the contractual reading.
Do not drop the 'tC' requirement or skip transfers with a missing C in partial scoring. That would weaken CHK-028/CHK-031.
